ground_truth_root_cause: Deploy cf3ba5c857d1 (2026-05-13T15:04:07Z) updated the Gradle ORM dependency (Hibernate) to a new major version and inadvertently changed the CartItem->ItemMetadata association fetch type from EAGER to LAZY in CartItem.java. This introduced an N+1 query pattern: loading a cart with N items now issues 1 query for cart_items followed by N individual SELECT queries against item_metadata (one per item, executed serially in a loop inside CartRepository.loadItemMetadata). Under normal load, carts with 10-15 items generate 11-16 DB queries per request instead of 2, rapidly saturating the 20-connection PostgreSQL pool and causing cascading HTTP 503 errors.
ground_truth_remediation: 1. Immediately roll back cart-service to the previous deploy (sha=2b8ccac18a70) to restore eager loading and relieve DB pool pressure. 2. Once service is restored, in CartItem.java revert the @ManyToOne fetch annotation from FetchType.LAZY back to FetchType.EAGER, or alternatively implement a JOIN FETCH query in CartRepository to load cart_items and item_metadata in a single query. 3. Add an index on item_metadata(item_id) if not present to reduce per-query latency. 4. Re-deploy the corrected version after verification in staging. Total estimated time: 30-60 minutes.
